newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-RUSSIAN WALKER STRIPPED OF MEDAL FOR DOPING.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-RUSSIAN WALKER STRIPPED OF MEDAL FOR DOPING.

text.p: Russian silver medallist walker Olympiada Ivanova became the second athlete to be stripped of a world championship medal for cheating with drugs on Sunday and faces a two-year ban from the sport.

Team sources said Ivanova, who finished second in Thursday's 10 kms walk, had tested positive for steroids together with compatriot Lyubov Tsyoma who failed to finish her 800 metres semifinal heat on the same day.

The 27-year-old Ivanova will also lose her $30,000 prize money. Under International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) rules, both athletes will be banned for two years, the minimum penalty for a serious doping offence.
Ivanova, who produced the best performance of her career to win the silver medal, was the second medallist to test positive after Ukraine's world shot put champion Aleksandr Bagach.

Bagach was stripped of his gold medal after testing positive for the stimulant ephedrine but escaped with a public warning because the drug is not regarded as being as serious an offence as steroid abuse.
French 400 metres hurdler Pascal Maran and women's triple jumper Oxana Zelinskaya of Kazakhstan, neither of whom made the finals, also tested positive for ephedrine and were given a warning.
The Athens championships have seen five positive cases so far and provided proof that athletes are still prepared to try to cheat their way to glory.

Under the IAAF's old rules the two Russians would have been banned for four years. But the IAAF decided to halve its bans for serious drugs at a meeting before the championships because of legal problems with the longer ban.
Belarus walker Olga Kardopoltseva, who finished third, will now be given the silver medal in the 10 kms with her compatriot Valentina Tsybulskaya elevated from fourth to the bronze medal position.
